title: I Need to Walk Along the Sidewalk...
text:
I need to walk along the sidewalk

somewhere

on a shady afternoon

find a table

on the terrace of a café

sit down

order a drink

and I want to sit there

with that drink

and I want

a fly to land

on that table.

Then

I want to see

a woman walk past

in a green dress.

I want to see pass by

a fat dog

with short brown hair and

smiling eyes.

I want to die

sitting there.

I want to die

upright

my eyes still

open.

I want an airplane

to fly overhead.

I want a woman

to pass by

in a blue dress.

Then I want

that same dog

with short brown hair and

smiling eyes

to walk past

again.

That will be

enough

after all the

other things

and all the

rest.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Charles Bukowski. The deliberately spare one-line stanzas and repeated phrasing are preserved.

title: Friendly Advice to a Bunch of Young People
text:
Go to Tibet.

Ride a camel.

Read the Bible.

Dye your shoes blue.

Grow a beard.

Sail around the world in a

Paper canoe.

Subscribe to the
Saturday Evening


Post
.

Chew only on the left side

Of your mouth.

Marry a woman with

One leg and shave with a

Razor.

And carve your names into her

Arm.

Brush your teeth with gasoline.

Sleep all day and climb the

Trees at night.

Be monks and drink buckshot and

Beer.

Keep your head underwater and

Play the violin.

Do the belly dance before

Pink candles.

Kill your dog.

Introduce yourselves to the mayor.

Live in a barrel.

Split your heads with an axe.

Plant tulips in the rain.

But do not write poetry.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Charles Bukowski. Odd capitalization, the split “Saturday Evening / Post” wording, punctuation, and lineation are retained as supplied.

title: Every So Often He Comes Back...
text:
every so often he comes back

to me,

there in his bed, blind,

being slowly consumed,

the little bulldog,

the nurses prowling, running

the curtains, the blinds, the sheets.

seeing whether he was still alive.

the boy from Colorado.

the courage of American Mercury.

the bad Catholic boy of Mencken.

who went to Hollywood.

and lay down on its shore.

consuming himself, consuming himself, consuming himself,

until he was gone.

he never knew he would be famous.

i wonder if he would have

cared.

i think he would.


John, this is your big moment.

you entered the books of

eternity

there beside Dostoevsky,

Tolstoy, and your little

Sherwood Anderson


I told you so.


and you said

“you wouldn’t shit on an old blind man,

would you?”

ah, there’s no need for that,

bulldog.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Charles Bukowski. Lowercase presentation, repetitions, quoted speech, and stanza spacing are preserved.

title: Embrace the Darkness
text:
Confusion is the god

madness is the god

the permanent peace of life

is the permanent peace of death…


Agony can kill

or it can sustain life

but peace is always horrible

peace is the worst thing

walking

talking

smiling

seeming to be

Do not forget the sidewalks,

the whores,

betrayal,

the worm in the apple,

the bars,

the prisons

the suicides of lovers.


Here in the United States

we have murdered a president and his brother,

another president had to leave office.


People who believe in politics

are like people who believe in God:

stroking air with bent

straws.


There is no God

there is no politics

there is no peace

there is no love

there is no control

there are no plans.


Stay away from God

remain anguished

slip away.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Charles Bukowski. The source’s colloquial voseo imperatives are rendered as direct English imperatives, and the lineation is preserved.

title: To the Bitch Who Took My Poems
text:
Some say we should remove from the poem

personal regrets,

remain abstract, there is some reason for this, but

God!

Twelve lost poems and I have no copies!

And you took my paintings too, the best ones!

It’s intolerable!

Are you trying to fuck me over like the others?

Why didn’t you take my money instead? Usually

they take it from the sick sleeping and drunken pants in the

corner.

Next time take my left arm or a

fifty-dollar bill,

but not my poems.


I’m not Shakespeare

but maybe one day I won’t write anymore,

abstract or otherwise;

There will always be money and whores and drunks

until the last bomb falls,

but as God said,

with his legs crossed:

“it seems I have created many poets

but not so much poetry.”
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Charles Bukowski. The profanity, direct address, quoted final lines, and stanza breaks are retained.

title: Air, Light, Time and Space
text:
“You know, I had a family, a job, something

was always

in the way

but now

I sold my house, found this

place, a large studio,

you should see the space and the light.


For the first time in my life I’m going to have the place

and the time to

create”


No, kid, if you’re going to create

you’re going to create while working

16 hours a day in a coal mine

or

you’re going to create in a tiny room with three kids

while you’re

unemployed,

you’re going to create even if part of your mind and

your body is missing, you’re going to create blind, maimed, crazy,

you’re going to create with a cat climbing up your

back while

the whole city trembles in earthquakes,

bombings, floods, and fire.


Kid, air, light, time and space

have nothing to do with this

and create nothing

except perhaps a longer life in which to find

new excuses.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Charles Bukowski. The conversational register, quotation marks, repeated “you’re going to create,” and lineation are preserved.

title: Someone
text:
Oh God, I had a terrible sadness,

that woman was sitting there and

told me:

are you really Charles Bukowski?

and I told her

let's leave that

I don't feel well

I have a tremendous sadness

and all I want is

to fuck you

she laughed

she thought I was acting

smart

and I was looking only at her long, thin

heavenly

legs

I saw her liver and her guts trembling

I saw Christ in there

dancing a folk dance.

All my inner lacks

rose up

and I went to her

and threw her down on the sofa

and lifted her dress to her neck

and I didn't give a damn

whether it was rape or the end of the world.

To be

there

again

in a

real

place

yes

her panties were on the

floor.

And my cock went in, my cock went in

oh God, my cock went in

I was Charles

Someone.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. Its fragmented free-verse layout and explicit, violent content are retained.

title: Some Dogs Sleeping at Night...
text:
Some dogs sleeping at night

must dream of bones

and I remember your bones

in the flesh

or better

in that dark green dress

and those high-heeled

black, shining shoes,

you always swore when

you were drunk,

your hair slipped from your ear

you wanted to explode

from what had trapped you:

rotten memories of a

rotten

past, and

in the end

you escaped

by dying,

leaving me with the

rotten

present.

You have been dead 28 years

and still I remember you

better than any

of the others

you were the only one

who understood

the futility of the

arrangement with life.

The others were only

uncomfortable with

trivial segments,

absurdly

criticized

the little things:

Jane, you

were murdered for knowing

too much.

Here is a drink

to your bones

that

this old dog

still

dreams of.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The ellipsis in the supplied title and the poem's spare lineation are retained.

title: Drunk Alice Yesterday...
text:
drunk Alice yesterday

gave me

a jar of fig jam

and today she

whistles

for her cat

but

he will not

come—

he is with the horses

in a

tub of beer

or

in room 21

of the

Crown Hill

Hotel

or he is in the

Cracker

Citizens National

Bank

or

arrived in

New York at

5:30 p.m.

with a paper suitcase

and

7 dollars.

near Alice

in her yard

a paper goose

walks

upside down

in a cardboard box that says:

California

Oranges.

the drunk Alice whistles.

not well not well.

work slowly.

everyone tries hard

but the

gods.

Alice goes in for a

drink, comes

out,

whistles again

all the way to a

park bench in

El Paso—

and her love comes

running from the

trees

eyes shining like a

color film

and not waiting

until

Monday

we go in

together.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The supplied opening phrase functions as a title, and its trailing ellipsis has been retained. The duplicated Spanish ‘vendrá / venir-’ is normalized by context as ‘will not / come—.’

title: I Gave a Poetry Reading Last Saturday At...
text:
I gave a poetry reading last Saturday in

the woods outside Santa Cruz

and was about to finish

when I heard a loud, long scream

and a fairly pretty young woman

ran toward me

long dress and fire in her eyes

and jumped onto the stage

and screamed: “I WANT YOU!

I WANT YOU! Eat me! Eat me!”

I told her, “hey,

leave me alone, fuck.”

But she kept taking off

my clothes and throwing herself

on me.

“Where were you,” I

asked, “when I had nothing

to eat and

sent stories to the

Atlantic Monthly?”

she grabbed my balls and nearly

tore them off. Her kisses

tasted like shit soup.

2 women jumped onto the stage

and

dragged her off

into the woods.

Her screams could still be heard

when I began the next poem.

Maybe, I thought, I should have

possessed her on stage in front

of all those eyes.

But you never know

if it would be a good poem or

a bad acid.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The ellipsis marks the supplied title's truncation; the body supplies the location and has been translated in full.

title: Not Blue
text:
She called me long-distance,

“you could never argue with me,”

she said,

“you always left.

my husband isn't like that,

he sticks to me like glue.

and he hits me.”

“I never believed in arguments,”

I said, “there's nothing to argue about.”

“you're wrong,” she said, “you should

try to communicate.”

“communicate is an overused word, like

love,” I told her.

“but don't you think two people can

love?” she asked.

“not if they try to communicate,”

I answered.

“you're talking like a fool,”

she said.

“we're arguing,”

I said.

“no,” she said, “we are trying to

communicate.”

“I have to go,” I said.

I hung up and took the phone off the hook.

I sat looking at it.

what they didn't understand was that

sometimes there is nothing to save

except the personal vindication of

one's own point of view

and that was what would cause

that blinding white flash

one of these days.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. “Plasticola” is rendered as “glue,” preserving the simile.

title: They Applaud Every Work...
text:
They applaud every work

without fail, without thinking

and four or five voices answer

in the same high pitch

“BRAVO! BRAVO!”

as if they had heard a new

and vital

creative explosion.

where have the audiences gone

that were able to choose and

discriminate?

what the collective mind of

the audience now thinks is:

we understand

we know

therefore

we respond

in unison.

and then

at the wheel of their automobiles

they rush out of the

underground parking lot

rougher and cruder

than any boxing crowd

than any racetrack crowd

cutting each other off

skidding

swearing.

The March to the Scaffold, of course

Pictures at an Exhibition, naturally

Bolero, yes

The Afternoon of a Faun?

honking

shooting along the freeways

BRAVO west L.A.

BRAVO Westwood Village

BRAVO Hollywood Hills

BRAVO Beverly Hills.

Pathetique Symphony, of course.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. Capitalization, repetitions, and named musical works are preserved.

title: Wrecked, Anchored, I Took Out Again...
text:
Wrecked, anchored, I took out again

the yellow notebook

I write from bed

as I did last

year.


I am going to the doctor

on Monday.

‘Yes, doctor, weak legs, dizziness,

headache and back

pain.’


‘Do you drink?’ he will ask me.

‘Do you do the exercises,

take the vitamins?’

I think I am simply sick

of life, always the same

stale fluctuating

factors.


Even at the racetrack

I watch the horses run

and it seems to me

that there is no point.


I leave right after betting

on the remaining races.

‘Are you leaving?’ the

clerk will ask me.

‘Yes, it is boring,’

I answer.


‘Look, if you think it is boring

out there,’ he tells me,

‘imagine in here.’


So here I am

propped up again on

the pillows.

Nothing but an old man

just an old writer

with a yellow

notebook.


Something is

coming across the

floor

toward me.


Ah, it is only my cat.

This time.—
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The closing ‘Algo sé / acerca por él / suelo / hacia mí’ contains two contextually clear stray accents; reading them as ‘Algo se / acerca por el / suelo / hacia mí’ yields ‘Something is coming across the floor toward me,’ confirmed by the following identification of the cat.

title: Roll the Dice
text:
if you're going to try, go all the way.

otherwise, don't even start.

if you're going to try, go all the way.

this could mean losing girlfriends,

wives,

relatives,

jobs and,

maybe your mind.

go all the way.

this could mean not eating for 3 or 4 days.

this could mean freezing on a park bench.

this could mean jail.

this could mean mockery, derision, loneliness...

loneliness is a gift.

the others are a test of your persistence, or

of how much you really want to do it.

and you will do it,

despite rejection and the disadvantages,

and it will be better than anything you imagined.

if you're going to try, go all the way.

there is no other feeling like that.

you will be alone with the gods

and the nights will blaze with fire.

do it, do it, do it.

do it.

all the way,

all the way.

you will ride life straight to the perfect laugh.

it is the only good fight there is.
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. Its repeated imperative and short free-verse lines are retained.

title: Beethoven Conducted His Last Symphony Completely Deaf
text:
His paintings would not be so valuable

now

if he had not

cut off his ear

put that rag around his head

and then killed himself

among the corn stalks.

would the poems of that other one

be so famous if he had not

disappeared at 19,

left everything to go

traffic arms and look for gold

in Africa only to

die of syphilis?

what about the one who was

murdered on the road

by Spanish fascists?

did that give

his words more

meaning?

or take that one who was a

national hero

those iceberg symphonies rising

cutting that particular sky

in two

he had everything handed to him

then he worried about old age

decided to save his head

went home

disappeared and was never seen

again.

what strange behavior, didn't someone say

once?

that a man must be as durable as his

art, that is what they expect, they demand the

impossible: creation and creator being the

same. this is the dirty trick

of every age
editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The title is retained despite the poem's allusive body; the source does not establish a title-body mismatch.
